verifications.claim: As of April 2026, the U.S. Postal Service (USPS) is temporarily suspending employer contributions to the Federal Employees Retirement System (FERS).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "suspending employer pension contributions for workers... affects the Federal Employees Retirement System (FERS)" (R1); "temporarily suspend its employer contributions to Federal Employees Retirement System annuities" (R2); "temporarily suspend employer contributions to the Federal Employees Retirement System" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state the suspension of USPS employer contributions to FERS in April 2026.

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Beginning April 10... Suspension of payments, effective April 10" (R3); "effective Friday, April 10" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state the effective date as April 10.

verifications.claim: The suspension aims to save approximately $2.5 billion through September 30.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "free up roughly $2.5 billion in the current fiscal year" (R1); "free about $2.5 billion in the current fiscal year" (R3); "save $2.5 billion with the action through Sept. 30" (R8)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm $2.5 billion savings in the current fiscal year (ending Sept. 30) or explicitly through Sept. 30.

verifications.claim: The suspension is by pausing $200 million in biweekly payments.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "about $200 million every two weeks" (R1); "about $200 million every other week" (R3); "$200 million payments every other week" (R8)
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly specify pausing biweekly or every-other-week payments of $200 million.

verifications.claim: Officials state there is no immediate impact on current or future retirees.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "no immediate impact on current or future retirees" (R1); "no immediate detrimental impact to our current or future retirees" (R3); "not be immediately impacted" (R2)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources quote officials stating no immediate impact on retirees.

verifications.claim: USPS is halting its employer contributions to the FERS defined benefit plan.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "employer’s contributions for the defined benefit portion of the Federal Employees Retirement System (FERS)" (R3); "employer contributions to FERS" as pension/annuity (R1, R2)
verifications.reasoning: Sources specify employer contributions to FERS defined benefit/pension plan.

verifications.claim: USPS will continue to transmit employee contributions to FERS.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "continue transferring employee payroll deductions into retirement accounts" (R1); "continue to transmit to OPM employees’ contributions to FERS" (R3); "continue to provide OPM with employees’ own contributions to FERS" (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state continuation of employee contributions to FERS.

verifications.claim: USPS will continue contributions to the Thrift Savings Plan (TSP).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "continue processing employee-funded contributions and matching funds into the Thrift Savings Plan (TSP)" (R1); "continue to transmit employer automatic and matching contributions... to the Thrift Savings Plan" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm continued TSP contributions, including employer matching.

verifications.claim: USPS will continue contributions to Social Security.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "maintain its employer contributions to Social Security" (R2); same in R9
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly state continuation of Social Security contributions.

verifications.claim: USPS reported $118 billion in net losses since 2007.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "totaling $118 billion since 2007" (R1); "net losses of $118 billion since 2007" (R6); same in R8
verifications.reasoning: Sources exactly match the $118 billion net losses since 2007 figure for USPS.

verifications.claim: USPS quarterly losses reached $1.25 billion in early 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "quarterly loss of $1.25 billion" in February (R6); "USPS in February reported a quarterly loss of $1.25 billion" (R8)
verifications.reasoning: Sources report exact $1.25 billion quarterly loss in February 2026 (early 2026).

verifications.claim: The Postal Service previously suspended these payments in 2011 during a similar financial crisis.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "deferred payments in 2011 during another financial crisis" (R2); "suspended its employer contributions to FERS in June 2011... during another acute period of financial stress" (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm prior suspension in 2011 during financial crisis.

verifications.claim: Career employees are covered under FERS or the Civil Service Retirement System (CSRS).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Career postal employees participate in one of two pension programs... CSRS or... FERS" (R7); "99 percent of career USPS employees are covered by... FERS" implying remainder CSRS (R2)
verifications.reasoning: Sources state career employees are under FERS or CSRS.

verifications.claim: USPS must fund its retirement obligations through its own operating revenue.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "The Postal Service does not [receive appropriations]. Instead, it's required to pay retirement contributions with agency revenue."
verifications.reasoning: R7 directly states USPS funds retirement from its own revenue, unlike other agencies.

verifications.claim: All three retirement-related funds (including health benefits) have unfunded liabilities.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "All three of its retirement-related funds have an unfunded liability... The Postal Service Retiree Health Benefits Fund (PSRHBF)"
verifications.reasoning: R7 explicitly states all three funds (CSRS, FERS, PSRHBF/health benefits) have unfunded liabilities.
